extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists) who need to compute Janet bases via the rstandard.lib library
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the SINGULAR library procedure rJanet which computes a Janet basis for a given ideal. Covers calling convention, inputs, outputs, purpose and an illustrative example showing expected output formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage: input is an ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rJanet(I); I is an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The single argument I must be an ideal object in SINGULAR. This documents the calling convention: rJanet takes the ideal (set of generators) as its sole input. Example in the text shows constructing a ring and an ideal, then calling rJanet(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Return: Janet basis (ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: ideal, a Janet basis for I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rJanet returns an ideal object representing a Janet basis for the input ideal I. The returned object is intended to be the Janet basis; in the example the result is assigned to 'j' and its elements are printed as j[1], j[2], ... The example also shows the routine prints the length of the basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: computes a Janet basis for any ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Computes a Janet basis for the ideal given by the generators in I for any ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure is intended to produce a Janet basis for the supplied ideal under arbitrary monomial/orderings supported by the ring definition. Users should set up the ring/ordering appropriately before calling rJanet. The doc references the procedure's origin (rstandard.lib) and its placement in the library documentation (Section D.15.33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: calling pattern and output format
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: LIB "rstandard.lib"; ring R= 32003,(a,b,c,d,e,f,g),dp; ideal i = <generators>; ideal j = rJanet(i); (cid:55)→ Length of Janet basis: 210 (cid:55)→ j[1]=... j[2]=... etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example demonstrates how to load the library, define a ring and ideal, call rJanet, and inspect the returned Janet basis. It shows that rJanet reports the length of the computed Janet basis and that basis elements are accessible as entries j[1], j[2], ... The large printed polynomials illustrate expected output verbosity and formatting. Use this example as a template for usage and for parsing the returned ideal/basis in scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library provenance / cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library rstandard.lib (see Section D.15.33 [rstandard lib], page 2215). See also: Section D.15.33.1 [borderBasis], page 2216.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation points users to the containing library (rstandard.lib) and related procedures (e.g., borderBasis). Users should consult the referenced sections for related algorithms, dependencies, or alternative basis computations.
